Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed graph implemented with adjacency lists, the cost of processing a vertex is proportional to its out-degree, which is bounded above by the maximum possible number of outgoing edges from any single vertex. The total cost across all operations in the sequence equals the total number of edges in the graph, since every edge is counted exactly once when its source vertex is processed.

* (a) The worst possible single operation has a cost of **|V| − 1**, which occurs when a vertex has an outgoing edge to every other vertex in the graph (assuming no self-loops in a simple directed graph).

* (b) The average amortized cost, computed via aggregate analysis, is **|E| / |V|**, since the sum of the costs of all |V| operations equals |E| (each edge contributes exactly once to the out-degree of its tail vertex), and dividing this aggregate total by the number of operations yields the amortized cost per operation.
